headline: The European Society of Cardiology has launched a 53-partner EU-funded network to test and share trusted AI tools for heart care across Europe.
score_reason: Sizeable official EU-backed initiative, but at launch stage with no results yet.
importance_line: Heart patients and hospitals across Europe could eventually get validated AI tools, but the network is only starting and its three-year roadmap is a hope, not a result.
source: European Society of Cardiology announcement, as carried by News-Medical
summary: News-Medical reports that the European Society of Cardiology is coordinating a new EU4Health-funded project, the European Cardiovascular Health Data and AI Network (CHAIN), a 36-month effort with 53 partners from 20 countries to connect hospitals and registries so AI heart-care tools can be tested and validated. Validated tools are to be listed in a European repository with 'AI Passports' recording their performance and safety, though the project has not yet produced results.
notes: Announcement text; credited to ESC as carried by News-Medical.
